findings.text: non-blocking: the reason assertion compares the recorded grant reason against the id the test itself supplied (repair.finding_id over the same finding), and in the single-finding case _grant_reason falls back to findings[0]['id'], which is that same id, so reverting the reason logic leaves this assertion true; the reason behaviour is actually guarded only by the two-finding test at line 156, whose `!= first['id']` does compare against an independent value.

non-blocking: the third asking pattern (`missing|uncommitted` ... `test`) matches any clause that carries one of those adjectives before the word test, so a finding about something else such as 'the uncommitted rename breaks the test suite' or 'the missing branch is uncovered by tests' is read as a test ask and grants a spurious tests/ path; the path grant is additive so this over-grants a write path rather than breaking the repair.
